title: Lightroom's mask Intersect: product or minimum?
note: Four flat grey frames, each labelled in its corner. Two crossing linear gradients darken them by a known amount, alone and intersected, so the masking agent can tell whether Lightroom intersects masks as a product or a minimum.

steps.title: Share the four frames to Lightroom
steps.detail: Each is a flat grey frame with its number in the top-left corner.

steps.title: Frame 0: no edits
steps.detail: Leave frame 0 as it is. It shows what Lightroom does to the grey without any mask.

steps.title: Frame 1: gradient A
steps.detail: Masking › Create New Mask › Linear Gradient. Drag from the left edge to the right edge, level. Set the mask's Exposure to −2.00 and nothing else.

steps.title: Frame 2: gradient B
steps.detail: A Linear Gradient dragged from the top edge to the bottom edge, straight down. The mask's Exposure −2.00, nothing else.

steps.title: Frame 3: A intersected with B
steps.detail: Make gradient A as on frame 1. On that mask, Intersect with a Linear Gradient dragged as on frame 2. Exposure −2.00 on the combined mask.

steps.title: Export all four
steps.detail: TIF if Lightroom offers it, otherwise JPG at quality 100. Full size, sRGB, no output sharpening, and keep the original file names.

steps.title: Share the exports back
steps.detail: Share the four exports to Redlamp Bench. They pair with their frames by file name.
